title: exakit
tagline: Your local Exasol database and everything that talks to it.

commands.summary: Check this machine's requirements; install nothing.
commands.description: Re-runs the machine-requirement checks the installer runs first - RAM, free disk, the container engine or the macOS runtime, and the ports the database needs - against an installed kit, and changes nothing. The same checks run before an install with EXAKIT_PREFLIGHT=1.

commands.summary: Is the database up and healthy?
commands.description: Shows what is installed, whether each component is healthy, which datasets are loaded, and whether add-on services are running. While the installer is still running the status is `installing` with the current step, exit 3, so a poll started in another shell can follow the install from its first seconds.

commands.summary: What is installed, and what is newer.
commands.description: Kit source and install date, then one row per component and add-on: what is installed, and whether the maintainers advertise something newer. Applying what is waiting is `exakit update`. --json prints the same rows as one object (installed, advertised, status, severity per component) with the installed/status/remedy keys every state query carries.

commands.summary: Your connection details.
commands.description: The connection panel: DSN, admin and MCP users, where each password file lives, TLS mode and paths. --json prints the install record (manifest.json) plus the state keys installed / status / remedy / skills on stdout, with nothing else on it.

commands.summary: Friendly walkthrough of every way to connect.
commands.description: How to connect AI clients over MCP, SQL clients (DBeaver or DbVisualizer), and Python via pyexasol.

commands.summary: Start the database and every add-on service, or one of them.
commands.description: Starts everything the kit runs, deploying the database first if it has never been deployed. Name a service to start only that one: database, or an installed add-on that runs a service (exakit status lists them under services). An add-on needs the database, so exakit start <add-on> refuses (exit 2) while the database is stopped and names the bare command. An unknown or uninstalled service is refused (exit 2) and nothing is started.

commands.summary: Stop the add-on services and the database, or one of them.
commands.description: Your data is kept. Bring it back with exakit start. Name a service to stop only that one - exakit stop exasol-scheduler leaves the database and every other add-on running; the bare command is the only form that stops the database without naming it. An unknown or uninstalled service is refused (exit 2) and nothing is stopped. A stopped add-on that is registered for automatic start comes back at the next login; exakit autostart is where that is turned off. exakit stop database asks first whether to stop the running add-on services too, because they need the database: yes stops them before it, no stops the database alone and names the exakit start <service> each needs once the database is back. EXAKIT_STOP_ADDONS=1 or 0 answers without a terminal; with neither, they are stopped too.

commands.summary: Come back automatically after a restart?
commands.description: Shows whether the kit's services start at login, then offers to change it.

commands.summary: Run one SQL statement, with the error translated.
commands.description: Runs a single statement and turns the three faults everyone hits first into their remedy (connection refused -> exakit start; FETCH FIRST/TOP -> LIMIT; object not found -> describe it). Reads only unless --write. A saved statement runs with --file <path> or on stdin; comment lines (--) and a trailing ; are dropped first. The remedy is printed FIRST, on stdout with the error. --json returns one object instead: {"ok": true, "rows": [...], "row_count": n} or {"ok": false, "error": ..., "remedy": <a command to run as written, or null>, "remedy_hint": <the explanation, or null>}, nothing else on stdout. remedy is only ever a runnable command (exakit start for connection refused, exakit status for a TLS fault); a fault with no command to run (object not found, FETCH FIRST/TOP) has remedy null and its advice in remedy_hint - read it, do not execute it; a refusal (typo, write without --write, two statements) is {"ok": false, "error": ..., "rejected": true} with exit 2. A first word that is neither a read nor a known write is reported as unrecognised (a typo), not as a write.
commands.warning: This connects with the starter-kit profile, which is the ADMIN user and is NOT sandboxed. The read-only boundary is the MCP user, not this command.
examples: exakit sql --json 'SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM TPCH.NATION'

commands.summary: Load sample data, one file, or a whole folder.
commands.description: Opens the data-loading menu: bundled datasets (tpch, energy, weather) or your own data. Name a path to skip the menu. A FILE asks the same two things whatever its kind - the file, then SCHEMA.TABLE - and JSON is shredded into tables by an engine the kit installs for you. A FOLDER is a bulk load: every CSV / Parquet / JSON (.json, .geojson) file at its top level, one table each named after the file, asking for the schema once. Files go to the loader as they are - a ';'-separated CSV with its delimiter, a header with no rows skipped by name, a tabular .txt or .tsv listed with the rename to .csv that exapump needs. Subfolders are not scanned, files of other kinds are ignored, and duplicates - byte-identical files, or two names that resolve to the same table - are skipped with the reason. RUNNING A FOLDER AGAIN IS SAFE: a file already loaded from that folder is skipped rather than loaded on top of itself, a file a stopped run left half-written is reloaded from scratch, and a target table holding rows this kit did not load is left alone unless you say otherwise (EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING). A SINGLE FILE is held to the same rule: a target already holding rows this kit did not load is not loaded unless EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING says replace (drop and rebuild it) or append (load on top) - on a terminal you are asked, and a declined load exits 5 with nothing changed - and the same file loaded twice is recognised and left as it is. When the load finishes, every file is listed with the table it went into, the rows it landed, and - for one that did not load - the reason against it; a file the engine refuses leaves no empty table behind. --force REPLACES bundled datasets instead of skipping what is already there: their tables are dropped and rebuilt, so anything you changed in those schemas is lost. JSON is macOS, Linux and WSL only; on Windows a folder's JSON files are listed as skipped. Unattended, EXAKIT_DATASETS=tpch,energy,weather loads only what is not loaded yet and exits 0 when everything named is already there.
environment: EXAKIT_DATASETS=tpch,energy,weather names exactly which bundled datasets to load
EXAKIT_DATA_FILE=/path/file.json or /path/folder answers the local-data question, so a run without a terminal loads that file or folder
EXAKIT_DATA_TABLE=SCHEMA.TABLE answers the target-table question for a single EXAKIT_DATA_FILE (default: STARTER_KIT.<filename>)
EXAKIT_SCHEMA sets the default target schema

EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING=skip|replace|append decides what happens to a target table that already holds rows this kit did not load, for a single file and for every file in a folder alike (default: skip, which is also the answer without a terminal; a declined single-file load exits 5 with nothing changed)

commands.summary: Every log the kit can show.
commands.description: The installer run, the database container, each add-on service, what the boot entries wrote at login, and the virtual-schemas day log (every SQL statement exakit connect and exakit source sent, secrets redacted; kept 14 days). No target lists them all with size and last-updated; -f follows one live; --path prints just the path for piping.

commands.summary: Connect your AI clients.
commands.description: Permanently configures the exasol MCP server in every supported AI client. Existing configs are backed up first. Restart the client afterwards and look for a server named exasol. Takes no options: clients are named with EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS (an option or argument exits 2). A client whose config no longer holds the kit's entry is offered again.
environment: EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS=claude,codex names clients by name (never menu numbers)

commands.summary: Test and repair the AI connection.
commands.description: Checks the configured MCP clients, repairs what has drifted - including a warning it can act on, such as a loosened file mode - then re-checks. Confirms the database is running first. --json reports the diagnosis without repairing; its remedy names this command. Each finding names the client it is about, and only that client reads needs_attention.

commands.summary: Show managed MCP state per client.
commands.description: Which clients the kit manages, which config file each one uses, and the current snapshot id. --json prints the operation result with a per-client state list (configured / not_set_up / not_installed).

commands.summary: Remove the kit's MCP entries from named AI clients.
commands.description: Takes the kit's managed entries (exasol, and an add-on's such as dash-server) out of the named clients and forgets them, so mcp-doctor stops reporting a client that is no longer on the machine. Clients by name (claude_desktop, claude_code, codex, cursor, vscode_copilot, gemini_cli, opencode, continue); the full removal is exakit uninstall.

commands.summary: List the AI skills the kit carries.
commands.description: One skill per component and add-on, with a one-line summary and whether each has reached the agents' discovery folders. Names the next command when one is needed: exakit update when the maintainers advertise a newer skill set, exakit skills-install when a placed skill has gone missing. The panel ends with one labelled tally (installed, arriving with an add-on, not placed, total), and --json carries the same four numbers under counts (installed, needs_addon, missing, total; they add up to total) beside installed_version, advertised_version, status and next.

commands.summary: Re-place the AI skills the kit copy carries (repair only).
commands.description: Places the skills this kit copy carries into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills, and merges the read-only command allowlist into Claude Code's settings. The installer already does this, and exakit update fetches and places a NEWER set, so this is only for a skill folder that went missing: exakit skills names it when that is the case. Restart or reload the agent afterwards.

commands.summary: Optional add-ons (dashboards and more).
commands.description: Browse and install optional tools: Space selects, Enter installs. Bare and without a terminal it installs NOTHING - installing non-interactively takes an explicit answer. --list shows every add-on and its state without installing anything (--json for scripts: one object whose addons array carries id, status, installed, version, repo and docs - the repository as owner/name and the documentation URL; version, repo and docs are null when unknown). The full reference for any add-on is on this machine: exakit help <id>. Naming ids installs exactly those: exakit marketplace dash-server. Installed add-ons then update through exakit update, and one can be removed with exakit uninstall <id>. A tool you installed yourself is recognised and never re-offered.
environment: EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS=dash-server answers the menu non-interactively (ids csv, all, or none)

commands.summary: Apply the updates that are waiting.
commands.description: Applies the quick components (kit scripts, exapump, MCP server, pyexasol, the AI skills, installed add-ons) in seconds. When the kit lists setup that only the installer can do and this machine has not finished it (a core task in setup/core/tasks.json, such as the SQL preprocessor framework), the downloaded installer is rerun once - none of the first install's questions again, every component kept at its installed version; with the database stopped that is deferred to exakit start && exakit update. An update that downloads a newer kit hands the rest of the run to it. When it cannot - the new exakit is missing or not executable, or on Windows, where the kit swap is usually staged for the moment the command exits - the run stops there instead: the rest is deferred (status deferred, remedy exakit update), so run exakit update again and the new kit applies it. Coming from 0.2.2, run exakit update twice. A newer skill set published by the maintainers is fetched and installed here too, with no kit release needed. A database change stops the database, so it is only applied for an answer the run was actually given: on a terminal you are asked, and an unattended run defers it with the exact command. Your data is kept either way. --yes (-y) may stand anywhere. --plan, --backup and --apply belong to the staged Personal major upgrade and work only with personal, as in exakit update personal --plan; written first, or with any other component, they are refused with the form that works. --json answers one object instead, with nothing else on stdout: {"ok", "status": updated|current|deferred|blocked|failed, "updated", "deferred", "blocked", "current", "skipped", "ahead", "failed", "remedy", "remedy_hint"}; every screen line goes to the log, nothing prompts, a database change is deferred unless --yes pre-answers it, and remedy names the command that applies what is left. Exit 1 when an updater failed. An unknown option or target is refused (exit 2) and records nothing.
environment: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE=1 pre-answers yes to the database change
EXAKIT_<COMPONENT>_VERSION pins one component by hand
EXAKIT_PERSONAL_S3=0 skips Exasol's S3 for the launcher and uses the GitHub release directly (for a network that blocks the bucket)

commands.summary: Rebuild a database that cannot start.
commands.description: For a deployment the launcher reports interrupted where every start fails the same way. Without --yes it asks, and without a terminal the answer is no: declining changes nothing and exits 5, so a scripted caller can tell "not confirmed" from "repaired". --json answers with one object ({"ok", "status", "changed", "remedy"}) instead of the panel.
commands.warning: DESTRUCTIVE: your database is rebuilt from empty and its data is not recoverable. Bundled datasets are reloaded afterwards.

exit_codes.5: declined - not confirmed, nothing was changed

commands.options: docker-nano [--container NAME] [--engine docker|podman] [--dsn HOST:PORT] [--user USER] [--password-file PATH] [--yes] [--json]
commands.summary: Copy an older kit's container database into this one.
commands.description: The installer asks about a container database from an older kit exactly once. This is for the machine that answered skip and wants the data after all, and for a container the installer never saw - made by hand with docker run exasol/nano, or by the upstream kit. Every non-system table is copied out while the container runs and restored into the running deployment with its column types preserved; the kit's own bundled sample data (tpch, energy, weather) is left out when it is unchanged, because the kit loads it itself (exakit data-load). When the container publishes the deployment's port, the database is stopped for the copy out and started again before the copy in; a container on another port costs no downtime. Nothing in the container is changed or removed. What is not named on the command line comes from the record the installer kept, then from the old install's own record, then from the machine (which engine knows the container, which port it publishes), then from an older kit's defaults (container exasol-nano, user sys). --json prints one object on stdout: ok, status (done | nothing | declined | failed | partial), container, engine, dsn, copied_out, restored, left_alone, failed, sample_left_out, reason, remedy.
commands.warning: The password never goes on the command line (there is no --password): pass a file with --password-file, set EXAKIT_LEGACY_PASSWORD for a scripted run, or answer the prompt on a terminal. A text column that held an empty string arrives as NULL.
environment: EXAKIT_LEGACY_PASSWORD=... the old database's password for a scripted run (a file via --password-file is preferred)
EXAKIT_LEGACY_READY_TIMEOUT=n seconds to wait for a container this command had to start (120)

exit_codes.0: done, or nothing of yours to copy
exit_codes.1: the copy did not finish - the reason and where the copies are kept are printed
exit_codes.3: no deployment to copy into, or no exapump to copy with
exit_codes.5: declined - not confirmed, nothing was changed

commands.summary: Remove what the kit installed.
commands.description: Pick what to remove (Skip, each add-on, or EVERYTHING) with a confirmation summary and a typed gate. --dry-run previews the full plan and changes nothing. Removing one add-on only: exakit uninstall <addon-id> [--yes] - the rest of the kit is untouched.
commands.warning: A full uninstall removes the database AND its data, the MCP configs, the skills and the binaries.

commands.summary: This screen.
commands.description: exakit help shows the everyday commands. --all lists every command. exakit help <component> (or exakit <component> --help) opens the full reference for one component.

commands.summary: Browse or search every command.
commands.description: Every exakit, exapump and exasol command in one searchable screen. --json prints the whole command surface as one machine-readable object.

commands.summary: What changed in this kit version.
commands.description: The what's-new card for the kit version you have installed, or for a named one. The installer shows the same cards, one per version crossed, after an upgrade; this prints them again any time.

commands.summary: Add the Kit 2 trust assets to this install (internal).
commands.description: Runs the kit's own upgrade/upgrade-kit2.sh against this install: the Trusted AI Workflow add-on is layered on top and nothing is reinstalled. An upgrade path the kit runs for itself, not a command to reach for by hand.

commands.summary: Remove exactly what upgrade-kit2 added (internal).
commands.description: Runs the kit's own upgrade/rollback-kit2.sh: everything upgrade-kit2 added is removed, and the database and every Kit 1 component stay untouched.

commands.summary: Query an external database from the local one (virtual schema).
commands.description: Connects PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks or MongoDB, Iceberg tables in AWS Glue - or document files in S3 or Azure Blob Storage - as an Exasol virtual schema: the tables stay at the source and queries fetch what they need. Search by name or alias (pg, mssql). On a terminal, `exakit connect` alone first names this computer's public IP (the address a source on the internet must allow), then opens a menu of the connectors by name (Space ticks several, Enter confirms; their adapter versions and tiers are in exakit source catalog), then one panel per source: first the source's connection string, pasted and read hidden like a password (Enter types the fields instead), then every field with its default, a required one marked with a red * (a plain * without colour) - Enter takes the default, a required field is never left empty - each answer checked where it is typed, and a numbered summary where a number asks that one answer again (- takes an optional one back). A plan that refuses one input goes straight back to that field; one naming several reopens the summary, where skip leaves that source out. A terminal without the panels asks the same questions line by line, marked the same way, the connection string first (hidden). A review shows what each will download and who can read it, and after one question a table follows every source to its VS_<NAME> or its failure; unattended, give every input with --set and the credential with --password-file or --password-stdin (never as an argument). --password-stdin reads all of standard input, line breaks included (a JSON key file), even when a terminal is open; a terminal or an empty stdin is refused (exit 2), and so is --password-stdin with --password-file. A --password-file or --password-stdin credential is read as UTF-8 (with or without a byte-order mark) or as UTF-16 by its byte-order mark, its trailing line endings dropped; anything else, a NUL byte included, is refused, never guessed. Windows PowerShell 5.1 pipes only ASCII to a command, so give a non-ASCII credential there with --password-file. --url takes the source's connection string (a JDBC URL, postgres://, mongodb+srv://, s3://, an Azure blob URL, ...) and fills the inputs it names, each checked as if given with --set; an explicit --set wins over it. A password in the string is never used or stored - the credential is still asked for separately - and settings the kit does not read are dropped by name. The adapter and JDBC driver are pinned and SHA-256 verified; the credential lives only in the database's CONNECTION EXAKIT_SRC_<NAME>, and the tables appear as VS_<NAME>. For a source on the internet the plan also names this computer's public IP address - the one its security group, firewall or IP access list must allow, since the database's traffic leaves through this computer (asked once of checkip.amazonaws.com, at most 3 seconds, never a step; --dry-run --json carries it as public_ip, null when not known) - and a connect or exakit source check that cannot reach the source names it in the fix. A failed connect leaves nothing behind. A source that moved (a new host, port or database) is re-pointed with the same command and its credential again: exakit connect <connector> --name <its name> --set host=<new host> --password-file <file> updates it in place - the recorded inputs stand and what is given replaces them, and VS_<NAME> keeps its name, so saved queries keep working. The credential is always required (a hidden prompt on a terminal, --password-file or --password-stdin unattended; without it, exit 2): the database never returns a stored one, and changing a CONNECTION's address clears it. The new address and credential are tried on a pending connection before anything changes, and any failure puts the source back as it was (exit 1, with the kind and fix); one interrupted part way is put back by the next command on the source. The plan shows each change, old -> new; a terminal asks (No by default), unattended it needs --yes, and --json without --yes changes nothing (exit 5, kind declined). The same inputs and no credential: nothing to change, exit 0 (1 when the source is not ready). A name another connector holds is a conflict (exit 3); a mapping, CA or TLS level is not changed in place, nor is a BigQuery source; a host of localhost is refused as for a first connect; a credential given with --set is refused (exit 2). The first connect installs the Java language container if it is missing (one database restart): at a terminal at once, picking the source being the permission; unattended only with --yes. --json prints one JSON object on stdout and nothing else, on every path: the plan with --dry-run, the connect result (action: connected, reconnected, repointed or unchanged; a re-point adds changes and credential: required in the plan, replaced in the result), or a failure {"ok": false, "error": <what happened>, "kind": <its class: input, conflict, gated, auth, tls, unreachable, nojava, ...>, "remedy": <the fix, in words>, "command": <the one exakit command that is the fix, or null>, "public_ip": ...} - the keys exakit source check --json answers with. It never asks: the credential comes from --password-file, from --password-stdin, or, on macOS and Linux, from standard input without the flag - read to its end, so a pipe that is closed once the credential is written; a stdin that stays open waits forever - and a missing language container is installed only with --yes. Exit 2 bad input, 3 name or object conflict, 5 connector gated or not confirmed (nothing changed), 20 Java in the database has no DNS resolver and the repair connect runs by itself (then one retry) did not fix it, 21 (Java) or 23 (Rust) a language container is missing and was not installed (--yes installs it), 22 the local database did not answer, 1 any other failure.
environment: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE=1 pre-answers the Java container install (--yes does the same)
EXAKIT_NO_IP_LOOKUP=1 skips the public IP lookup (no request to checkip.amazonaws.com)
examples: exakit connect pg --name sales --set host=db.example.com --set database=sales --set user=reader --password-file ~/.sales.pw
pass show db/sales | exakit connect pg --name sales --set host=db.example.com --set database=sales --set user=reader --password-stdin --yes --json

commands.options: list|issues [--status S]|catalog|show N|describe N [TABLE] [--ddl] [--schema S]|check N|--all|reauth N [--password-file F | --password-stdin]|refresh N|disconnect N|remove N [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]
commands.summary: List, check and manage connected external sources.
commands.description: list shows saved sources: where each lives, its TLS level (verify, require or disable) and its last known state (--json rows carry host and tls); issues filters the failing ones with the command that fixes each; check runs a fresh bounded read through the adapter (--all for every source, one shot, not monitoring); reauth replaces the credential from a hidden prompt, --password-file or --password-stdin (all of standard input, as exakit connect reads it) and reads again; refresh re-reads the source's table list; describe lists its tables and columns as Exasol sees them, read from the local catalog without reaching the source, and --ddl prints CREATE TABLE statements (with --schema, for that schema) to copy a table locally; disconnect drops only the CONNECTION (queries fail until you connect again with the same name); remove drops the virtual schema, adapter and connection and deletes the downloaded files no other source still uses. disconnect and remove preview first and ask; --dry-run only previews, and without a terminal or with --json they need --yes (unconfirmed: exit 5, nothing changed; with --json the answer is kind declined and command names the --yes form). reauth tries the new credential before it replaces the old one. Remote data is never touched.
examples: exakit source describe sales orders --ddl --schema LOCAL > orders.sql

environment.name: EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS
environment.effect: Which MCP clients to configure, by name: claude, claude_desktop, claude_code, codex, cursor, vscode_copilot, gemini_cli, opencode, continue, all, skip.

environment.name: EXAKIT_DATASETS
environment.effect: Which bundled datasets to load: tpch, energy, weather.

environment.name: EXAKIT_LOAD_SAMPLE
environment.effect: 0 skips data loading, 1 loads the bundled sample.

environment.name: EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS
environment.effect: Answers the marketplace offer: ids csv, all, or none.

environment.name: EXAKIT_REUSE_DB
environment.effect: 1 adopts an existing database (default), 0 destroys it and deploys fresh - 0 removes the local deployment and all its data.

environment.name: EXAKIT_DB_PORT
environment.effect: Alternate database port. The launcher selects and remembers the deployment's own port; exakit info shows the one in use.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VERSION_POLICY
environment.effect: manifest (default), latest, or pinned - where component versions come from.

environment.name: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE
environment.effect: 1 pre-answers yes to stopping the database for a runtime update.

environment.name: EXAKIT_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE
environment.effect: 1 never prints the update notice other commands can show.

environment.name: EXAKIT_NO_IP_LOOKUP
environment.effect: 1 skips the public IP lookup exakit connect and exakit source check make for a source on the internet (one HTTPS request to checkip.amazonaws.com, at most 3 seconds); the plan and the fix then do not name the address.

environment.name: EXAKIT_PERSONAL_S3
environment.effect: 0 skips Exasol's S3 bucket for the Personal launcher and downloads the verified GitHub release directly - for a network that blocks the bucket. Default: S3 first, GitHub as fallback.

troubleshooting.symptom: Podman is installed but not running
troubleshooting.remedy: Run: podman machine start - then re-run the installer.
Stop the other app, or re-run with EXAKIT_DB_PORT=8564.
Re-run the same install command. It resumes from the failed step.
exakit status, then exakit mcp-doctor, then restart the AI client.

troubleshooting.symptom: Another setup run is already in progress
troubleshooting.remedy: Wait for it. If the pid is dead, remove ~/.exasol-starter-kit/.install.lock and re-run.
exakit logs has the full story. Every error message names its remedy.
